ash: Weird one: anchor link to the "Using shortcuts" section jumps to the inline <kbd> shortcut element instead of the H2. Seen on staging and prod. PR: https://git/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2578
mike: can you paste the minimal markdown?
ash: sure:

```markdown
## Using shortcuts
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> to open command palette.
[Go to Using shortcuts](#using-shortcuts)
```

ash: link lands at the first <kbd> element. Looks like the slug generator is picking up the raw inline HTML tag and creating an identical id on the element.
sophia: hmm. inline HTML nodes can produce ids when they're the first element or have attributes. our slugifier should ignore HTML tags when computing heading slugs.
mike: short fix: add explicit id to heading: `## Using shortcuts {#using-shortcuts}`. also a tiny note in the PR explaining why.
ash: pushed the id patch to PR #2578.
docsys-bot: Reminder: docs style guide update suggestion - "avoid inline HTML inside first line of heading blocks; use escaping or explicit ids"
ci-bot: CI: docs/linkcheck started for PR #2578
ci-bot: CI: linkcheck failed (anchor mismatch) - see job log
sophia: I'll open DOCS-861 to update our slugifier to strip inline HTML and add a linkcheck assertion that anchors point to headings, not arbitrary inline nodes.
mike: also consider a lint rule that flags inline HTML snippets at the start of a paragraph or immediately under a heading. cheap and prevents these slips.
ash: CI re-run after my patch
ci-bot: CI: linkcheck passed for PR #2578 \u2705
sophia: filing follow-up PR to add the lint rule and a unit test for slug normalization. Assigning DOCS-861 to docs infra.
ash: thanks, merging now. :shipit:
